Benthic Ecology

The Antarctic seafloor and its inhabitants (the benthic ecosystem) are affected by a changing physical environment, including warming and acidifying oceans, sea-ice loss, ice shelf retreat, and extreme weather events. These changes will result in winners and losers among ecologically important benthic species, which in turn will alter marine biodiversity and food webs. Studying this ‘living laboratory’ provides insights on potential impacts of climate change, and informs ecosystem protection and management.

Dave Windy Planking

Dave Langrish at New Zealand's Scott Base has gone the extra mile—literally and figuratively—by raising funds for Canteen, a charity supporting young people impacted by cancer in New Zealand. What makes this effort even more impressive? Dave had never really planked before taking on this challenge! 

Dave started a Give Little (NZ) page in October for his 'Antarctic Plank Challenge' with a target of planking for 20 minutes. By 9 December, he had pushed that out to 1 hour and six minutes.

His efforts were even featured on Wednesday 10 December on TVNZ's Seven Sharp, shining a spotlight on the incredible things that can happen when purpose meets perseverance.

Dave’s role at Scott Base is ‘field support’ his team provides practical support to scientists and others working in the field. They keep us all alive in one of the most extreme environments on the planet!

You can give a shout out to the man with a heart of gold and abs of steel by donating here:  
https://givealittle.co.nz/fundraiser/antarctic-plank-challenge?ref=home&ref_code=donation_feed

The challenge closes on 23 December.

Sea ice REEL

This short video summarises research into sea ice undertaken by the Antarctic Science Platform over seven years. Changing Antarctic sea ice has global consequences. Since 2016, Antarctic sea ice has sharply and unexpectedly declined, likely due to combined effects of changes in the ocean, atmosphere, and winds. Understanding and monitoring changes in sea ice is crucial. This knowledge is needed to project future sea-ice behaviour and to understand the complex interactions between the ocean, atmosphere, ice, and ecosystems.
More information can be found here:
https://www.antarcticscienceplatform.org.nz/impactportfolio/declining-antarctic-sea-ice

CRL Tunnel Vision December 2025

Tēnā koe,
As we close out the year, this edition of Tunnel Vision looks back on the significant progress made on the City Rail Link project.
 
In 2025, we hit many major milestones, from the first successful test train journey through the CRL tunnel at the start of the year, to the completion of Beresford Square at Karanga-a-Hape and the re-opening of Albert Street to buses.
 
Inside the stations, distinctive architectural and cultural features such as the kaitiaki at Te Waihorotiu and the kauri snails at Mercury Lane were unveiled throughout the year, marking visible progress as the project moves steadily toward completion.
 
With these milestones behind us, we look forward to welcoming Aucklanders on board in the second half of 2026.
 
From all of us at City Rail Link, we wish you a safe and relaxing Christmas and a happy New Year!

Building skills, building confidence, building a future!

We’re sharing an awesome kōrero with Max Elsmore, Apprentice Builder with Brendan Fry Builder Limited and a graduate of the NZ Certificate in Construction (Level 3).

We also hear from Brendan Fry, Max’s boss, who shares his perspective on the value of training, the importance of hands‑on learning, and what makes Max a great fit for the team.

If you’re thinking about a career in construction or want to get started in the trades, Max’s journey, backed by an employer who believes in growing talent, shows just how many opportunities open up when you take that first step.

We hosted a webinar on 1 December 2025 about what's needed to improve crisis responses across Aotearoa New Zealand.

The hour-long webinar included a Q + A with our panelists:
- Sonya Russell, Kaiwhakahaere Hauora Hinengaro, Waranga | Director Mental Health and Addiction Sector Leadership, Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission
- Kerri Butler, Director, Take Notice
- Dr Leeanne Fisher, National Chief Mental Health and Addiction, Heath New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora

This webinar was the third in a series run by Te Hiringa Mahara about our programme of work examining effective crisis response systems, focused on our recently released monitoring report which calls for the development of a nationally cohesive approach to crisis responses.

Te Kanapu Technical Approach webinar

Te Kanapu is Transpower's initiative to create a future grid blueprint for Aotearoa, to support economic growth and the drive for a net zero 2050.

As part of the development of the grid blueprint, Transpower published on 10 December 2025 a suite of documents outlining the technical approach they are using in this work.

This webinar, held on 11 December 2025, provides an overview of this document suite.

You can read an executive summary of the technical approach, and access the full suite of documents, at www.transpower.co.nz/our-work/te-kanapu/technical-approach.
